messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Incident 4312109999 detected: repeated OOMs on serving-runtime group kv-paged-alloc across 3 nodes. Auto-escalation triggered. Affected service: inference-runtime (text-gen).

maya: I’m on it. seeing node flaps in metrics, memory climb ~= 30MB/min on kv cache allocator. Correlates with longer seq workloads.

cheng: logs show repeated `cudaMemoryAlloc` failures right before container restart on node gpu-05. snippet: 
```
E 04:12:07 runtime.cu: cudaMemoryAlloc failed: out of memory
E 04:12:07 allocator.cc: attempted alloc 8MB, failed, triggering oom-kill
I 04:12:08 containerd: container runtime restart (exit code 137)
```

maya: customer impact? any 5xx spikes or user-visible latency?

lucy: front line: 502s for ~2% of requests in us-west-2, spikes on the text-gen /v1/chat route. Most retries succeed against fallback model but tail latency up. Ticket #INC-1889 opened by customer-ops.

oncall-bot: paging @maya, @cheng, @lucy per oncall rota. Runbook: "Paged KV allocator leak" recommended mitigation steps.

akshay: quick triage: looks like slow fragmentation (pages not being reclaimed) rather than instant leak. KV page bitmap shows many semi-resident pages marked free but with stale refs -> prevents defrag.

maya: ok do we have a safe live mitigation? suggestions: 1) reduce per-request kv cache retention (prefix TTL) 2) temporarily lower batch sizes 3) force a rolling restart of affected replicas 4) trigger defrag/compact if runtime exposes it.

cheng: runtime exposes `--kv-compact` but it’s heavy and pauses serving for ~200ms. prefer rolling restarts across AZ to avoid full outage. I'll try lowering retention first.

lucy: I can flip retention config via configmap for the dedicated pool. patch: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch configmap kv-config -p '{"data":{"kv_retention_ms":"60000"}}'
```
I'll apply to us-west-2 staging first then prod if green.

maya: while lucy patches, akshay, can you watch GPU mem histograms and eviction rates? set alert for mem growth > 20MB/min.

akshay: watching. setting a temporary alert rule now.

deploy-bot: rollout triggered by lucy: configmap/kv-config patched on deployment inference-prod-usw2 (5/10 pods updated).

cheng: noticing `cudaMemoryAlloc` errors drop after retention reduced on two pods. one pod still flapping (gpu-05). I've scheduled a controlled restart for that pod to force KV reset.

maya: go ahead with restart; prefer drain -> restart -> uncordon. command?

cheng: running: 
```bash
kubectl drain gpu-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data && kubectl delete pod inference-runtime-gpu-05 && kubectl uncordon gpu-05
```

cheng: pod restarted. logs show it recovered, no immediate OOM. mem growth still present but much slower.

lucy: config change rolled to all 10 pods. latency and 5xx rate improving; customer-ops updated ticket: partial mitigation, fallback still triggered but fewer requests impacted.

maya: we need a postmortem plan and a long-term fix: options: a) improve allocator defrag heuristics + periodic compaction b) add background slab scavenger c) expose safe compact API for live compaction d) hard cap per-request kv retention and dynamic scaling by seq length.

akshay: logging shows compaction was not invoked for >48h due to a bug in the compaction scheduler when ephemeral page churn crosses threshold. I’ll file a follow-up PR with tests.

maya: assign follow-ups: akshay -> compaction scheduler bug + tests (P0), cheng -> add graceful compact endpoint and rate-limiting (P1), lucy -> add a canary config to autoset lower kv retention on high seq traffic (P1). I'll start incident write-up and customer summary.

maya: handoff to SRE rotation @sre-oncall for overnight monitoring. Please keep alert thresholds and escalate if mem growth resumes.

sre-oncall: acknowledged. I’ll keep watch and notify if we see >2 nodes with mem growth >15MB/min or any restart surges. Also capturing heap snapshots from next recurrence.

lucy: customer-ops updated: "We observed elevated 502s between 04:10-04:50 UTC for a small percentage of requests. Incident mitigated by config change and pod restart. No data loss. We will provide timeline + RCA." :thumbsup:

maya: final note: retro action — add a runtime health endpoint to expose page fragmentation metrics so oncall can triage faster. Adding to backlog.

incident-bot: Incident 4312109999 status changed to "mitigated" by maya at 04:52 UTC. Postmortem requested.

maya: wrapping up, will draft postmortem and send to #incidents. If anyone sees recurrence ping this thread. Thanks all. :heart:
